main_point.en: When we face the reality of physical death, we can cling to the hope of eternal life.
main_point.zh-Hant: 面對肉身死亡的現實時，我們可以緊緊抓住永生的盼望。

christ_connection.en: When Jesus raised the widow’s son from the dead, He showed that He has power over death. Jesus said, “I am the resurrection and the life” (John 11:25). Because Jesus died on the cross and rose from the dead, we have full assurance that Jesus will one day defeat death forever and resurrect us from the dead.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 耶穌使寡婦的兒子從死裏復活時，顯明了祂有勝過死亡的能力。耶穌說：「復活在我，生命也在我。」（約翰福音 11:25）因為耶穌在十字架上受死並從死裏復活，我們完全確信祂有一天會永遠戰勝死亡，並使我們從死裏復活。

title.en: Death Is the Effect of Sin

content.en:
11 Soon afterward he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a great crowd went with him. 
12 As he drew near to the gate of the town, behold, a man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow, and a considerable crowd from the town was with her. 
13 And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Do not weep.”
content.zh-Hant:
11 過了不多時，耶穌往一座城去，這城名叫拿因，他的門徒和極多的人與他同行。
12 將近城門，有一個死人被抬出來。這人是他母親獨生的兒子；他母親又是寡婦。有城裏的許多人同著寡婦送殯。
13 主看見那寡婦，就憐憫她，對她說：「不要哭！」

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌有勝過死亡的權柄

content.en:
14 Then he came up and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still. And he said, “Young man, I say to you, arise.” 
15 And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother. 
16 Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and “God has visited his people!” 
17 And this report about him spread through the whole of Judea and all the surrounding country.
content.zh-Hant:
14 於是進前按著槓，抬的人就站住了。耶穌說：「少年人，我吩咐你，起來！」
15 那死人就坐起，並且說話。耶穌便把他交給他母親。
16 眾人都驚奇，歸榮耀與神，說：「有大先知在我們中間興起來了！」又說：「神眷顧了他的百姓！」
17 他這事的風聲就傳遍了猶太和周圍地方。

content.en: Leaders: You and your students have likely walked through grief. Take comfort in knowing that Jesus is moved by our grief and cares for our sorrow (Luke 7:13).
content.zh-Hant: 領袖：你和學生很可能都曾經歷悲傷。知道耶穌因我們的悲傷而動憐憫的心，也關心我們的哀痛，願這事實安慰你們（路加福音 7:13）。

title.en: Death Is the Effect of Sin

content.en: “Since Jesus addresses the son as ‘young man’ (v. 14), we may assume that the woman has been left alone at a relatively young age. She lived in a man’s world in which a woman had no legal rights. The testimony of women and slaves was unacceptable in judicial proceedings. Thus a woman without a man to represent her was particularly helpless and defenseless. The Gospels testify that Jesus had ‘compassion’ on people like this.”⁵
content.zh-Hant: 「由於耶穌稱呼兒子為『少年人』（第 14 節），我們可以推想這婦人在相對年輕的時候就獨自一人了。她生活在一個由男人主導的世界，婦女沒有法律權利。婦女和奴僕的證詞在司法程序中不被接納。因此，沒有男人代表的婦女特別無助，也無法保護自己。福音書見證耶穌『憐憫』這樣的人。」⁵

content.en: “She has already buried her husband. Perhaps the son’s tone of voice, physical appearance, and gestures were reminders of her dearly departed spouse. So now all that existed of that former life heads to the grave. And, with no husband and no son, she had no way of providing for herself in that culture and time. She’ll soon be alone. Perhaps that’s why ‘a large crowd from the city was also with her.’ It’s like the entire community knew what grief and difficulty lay ahead.”⁶
content.zh-Hant: 「她已經埋葬了丈夫。也許兒子的聲調、外貌和舉止都使她想起心愛的亡夫。如今，昔日生活所剩的一切也要進入墳墓。沒有丈夫，也沒有兒子，在當時的文化和時代中，她無法養活自己。她很快就要孤身一人了。也許這就是為甚麼『有城裏的許多人同著寡婦送殯』。彷彿整個社區都知道前面有多少悲傷和艱難等待著她。」⁶

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌有勝過死亡的權柄

content.en: “Some commentators have seen a close link between this story and a similar one in the Old Testament where a non-Israelite widow at Zarephath had her son restored to life by the prophet Elijah (1 Kings 17:8-24). At the end of that account, the widow told Elijah: ‘Now I know for sure that you are a man of God, and that the LORD truly speaks through you’ (1 Kings 17:24). The successful prophetic intervention had convinced her of the prophet’s authenticity. Similarly, in the Gospel story, the people declared, ‘A mighty prophet has risen among us’ (7:16).”⁷
content.zh-Hant: 「有些註釋家認為，這個故事與舊約中一個類似的故事密切相關：撒勒法的一位非以色列寡婦的兒子藉著先知以利亞得以復活（列王紀上 17:8-24）。在那個故事的結尾，寡婦對以利亞說：『現在我知道你是神人，耶和華藉你口所說的話是真的。』（列王紀上 17:24）先知成功地介入，使她確信他是真先知。同樣，在福音書的故事中，百姓宣告：『有大先知在我們中間興起來了』（7:16）。」⁷

content.en: When Jesus met this widow in the town of Nain, women had little rights and few choices to earn a living. Men not only provided financially for the women in their lives, but they also provided physical and legal protection. A woman’s testimony wasn't accepted in court, so if facing legal accusations, widows were completely defenseless. Once her husband died, the widow’s son would’ve cared for, provided for, and protected her. So, when Jesus stepped onto the scene, the widow in this passage was mourning so many losses: the death of her son, the death of her security, and the death of life as she knew it—again. The townspeople would’ve known her situation and likely had sympathy for her, but they could do nothing to make it better. Thankfully, Jesus could and did. And this isn’t the only place we see Jesus care for the women in His day: He offered hope and forgiveness to a Samaritan woman who was looked down on and treated as an outcast by the Jews (John 4); He stood up for a woman caught in adultery, keeping her from being stoned to death and offering grace instead John 8:2-11); He included women in His ministry and even appeared first to a group of women after His resurrection. Once again, we see that Jesus often discarded cultural norms in favor of loving people and inviting them to experience salvation.
content.zh-Hant: 耶穌在拿因城遇見這位寡婦時，婦女幾乎沒有權利，謀生的選擇也很少。男人不但供養家中的婦女，也為她們提供人身和法律上的保護。婦女的證詞不被法庭接納，因此寡婦若面對法律指控，便完全無法為自己辯護。丈夫去世後，寡婦的兒子會照顧、供養和保護她。因此，當耶穌來到時，這段經文中的寡婦正在為許多失去哀傷：兒子的死亡、保障的消失，以及她所熟悉的生活再次結束。城裏的人都知道她的處境，也很可能同情她，卻無法改善她的情況。感謝神，耶穌能，而且祂做到了。這也不是我們唯一一次看見耶穌關心祂那時代的婦女：祂把盼望和赦免賜給一位被猶太人輕看、排斥的撒馬利亞婦人（約翰福音 4 章）；祂為一位被抓到行淫的婦人挺身而出，免她被石頭打死，反而向她施恩（約翰福音 8:2-11）；祂讓婦女參與祂的事工，復活後甚至首先向一群婦女顯現。我們再次看見，耶穌常常打破文化常規，選擇愛人，邀請他們經歷救恩。

content.en: Both the Old and New Testaments teach that one day believers will experience a resurrection of the body from the dead (Isa. 26:19; Ezek. 37:12-14; John 11). The promise of the resurrection is found in the resurrection of Christ from the dead, and it will take place at the future return of Christ. Because Christ was resurrected, Christians can be assured that their resurrection will be similar in nature, meaning it will be both bodily and glorious (Phil. 3:20-21; Rom. 8:22-23). The hope of the future resurrection gives believers confidence that death has been defeated in the death and resurrection of Christ.
content.zh-Hant: 舊約和新約都教導，信徒有一天會經歷身體從死裏復活（以賽亞書 26:19；以西結書 37:12-14；約翰福音 11 章）。復活的應許以基督從死裏復活為根據，並將在基督將來再來時實現。因為基督已經復活，基督徒可以確信，他們的復活在性質上與祂相似，也就是身體復活，並且充滿榮耀（腓立比書 3:20-21；羅馬書 8:22-23）。將來復活的盼望使信徒確信，死亡已在基督的受死和復活中被戰勝。

content.en: LORD JESUS, WHEN WE’RE HURTING OVER LOSS AND GRIEF, REMIND US OF THE HOPE WE HAVE IN YOU. HELP US TO SUPPORT ANY STUDENTS WHO MAY BE GRIEVING, OFFERING THEM THE SAME HOPE AND COMFORT YOU HAVE GIVEN US.
content.zh-Hant: 主耶穌，當我們因失去和悲傷而傷痛時，求祢提醒我們在祢裏面的盼望。幫助我們支持可能正在哀傷的學生，把祢賜給我們的同樣盼望和安慰帶給他們。

content.en: On a scale of 1-10 (1=Not at all; 10=Completely), how much of a rule follower are you?
content.zh-Hant: 從 1 到 10 分（1＝完全不遵守；10＝完全遵守），你有多遵守規則？

title.en: Consequences And Loss Supplies List: None
title.zh-Hant: 後果與失去　用品清單：無

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You'll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些選擇性活動旨在幫助學生互動。其中包括討論活動和文化連結，後者涉及當今青少年文化中的相關話題。每個小組都不同，請調整活動以配合你的小組需要。目標是讓學生藉著與主題及彼此建立連結，更投入這課的內容。

請提出以下問題，並給學生時間分享答案：

question.en: WHAT KINDS OF CONSEQUENCES DO YOUR PARENTS OR GUARDIANS GIVE FOR BREAKING THEIR RULES?
question.zh-Hant: 如果你違反父母或監護人訂立的規則，他們會如何處分你？

question.en: WHEN HAVE YOU LOST SOMETHING YOU VALUED—EVEN A DREAM YOU HELD?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾在甚麼時候失去過珍視的東西，甚至是懷抱的夢想？

question.en: WHEN HAVE YOU LOST PEOPLE YOU LOVED, EITHER THROUGH BROKEN RELATIONSHIPS OR DEATH?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾在甚麼時候因關係破裂或死亡而失去所愛的人？

content.en: When we break rules, we face consequences. This reality is just as true today as it was for Adam and Eve in Genesis. When they broke God’s rules for living with Him in Eden, sin entered the world—and so did disorder, sickness, and death. But the biggest loss that day was their close relationship with God. Thankfully, because of Jesus, who has power and authority over everything, we have hope that sin and death are not the end.
content.zh-Hant: 我們違反規則時，就要面對後果。今天的現實與創世記中亞當和夏娃所面對的一樣。當他們違反神為他們在伊甸園與祂同住所訂的規則時，罪進入了世界，混亂、疾病和死亡也隨之而來。但那天最大的損失，是他們與神親密的關係。感謝神，因著有能力和權柄勝過一切的耶穌，我們有盼望：罪和死亡並非終結。

cultural_connection.en: None of us fully understand why bad things happen. We ask, “If God is good, why does evil exist? Why hasn’t Jesus come back already? Why do people die—‘good’ people, young people, and those who still have so much to give to the world?” Knowing the answers wouldn’t take our pain away, but we struggle with these questions anyway because we want a reason for the pain. Ultimately, we want to know God’s heart. While God’s mind and plans are so far above anything we can understand (Isa. 55:8-9), we can trust a few general truths about God: God is good. Since God is good, He allows us free will, and sometimes we choose sin and evil. Since God is good, His timing seems slow because He wants more people to experience His grace, mercy, and forgiveness (2 Pet. 3:9). Since God is good, He invites us to trust Jesus for salvation and promises that we’ll spend eternity with Him—and all other believers who have died before us. He is good. And one day, all that is wrong and evil will come undone because of His goodness.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 我們沒有人能完全明白為甚麼壞事會發生。我們會問：「如果神是良善的，為甚麼邪惡存在？為甚麼耶穌還沒有回來？為甚麼人會死——包括『好人』、年輕人，以及仍有許多可以貢獻給世界的人？」知道答案不會消除我們的痛苦，但我們仍然為這些問題掙扎，因為我們想知道痛苦的原因。歸根究底，我們想認識神的心。雖然神的意念和計劃遠超過我們所能理解的（以賽亞書 55:8-9），我們可以相信幾項關於神的基本真理：神是良善的。因為神是良善的，祂賜給我們自由意志，而我們有時會選擇罪和邪惡。因為神是良善的，祂的時間看似緩慢，是因為祂想讓更多人經歷祂的恩典、憐憫和赦免（彼得後書 3:9）。因為神是良善的，祂邀請我們信靠耶穌得救，並應許我們將與祂，以及所有先我們離世的信徒共度永恆。祂是良善的。有一天，因著祂的良善，一切錯誤和邪惡都會被消除。

title.en: Death Is The Effect Of Sin

question.en: What details does Luke give us about the woman in Nain (v. 12)? How do they help us see the effects of sin on the world?
question.zh-Hant: 路加提供了哪些有關拿因城那位婦人的細節（第 12 節）？這些細節如何幫助我們看見罪對世界的影響？

answer.en: Leaders: Share context on widows. Can you imagine this woman’s grief? Not only had she buried her husband, but now she was burying her only son. She was alone, despite being surrounded by several people from her town. Sin’s effect means that we all eventually know what it’s like to grieve or to feel completely alone, even when we’re with other people. Their presence is helpful but doesn’t take away the pain. The people from the widow’s town could mourn with her, but they couldn’t give her what she needed—only Jesus could. Thankfully, He was already moving toward her.
answer.zh-Hant: 領袖：請分享有關寡婦的背景資料。你能想像這位婦人的悲傷嗎？她不但埋葬了丈夫，現在還要埋葬獨生子。儘管城裏有許多人圍繞著她，她仍是孤單的。罪的影響意味著，我們最終都會知道哀傷或感到完全孤單是甚麼滋味，即使身邊有人也是如此。他們的陪伴雖然有幫助，卻不能消除痛苦。城裏的人可以與寡婦一同哀哭，卻不能給她所需要的——只有耶穌能。感謝神，祂已經向她走來。

question.en: Which title did Luke use to refer to Jesus in verse 13? Why do you think he chose that title here?
question.zh-Hant: 路加在第 13 節用甚麼稱號指耶穌？你認為他為甚麼在這裏選用這個稱號？

answer.en: Because of sin, death is a part of life for everyone, so Jesus passing this funeral procession isn’t surprising. But for the widow, everything changed on this day. Life kept moving while she grieved, but Jesus didn’t. Jesus saw her, stopped for her, and showed that He is Lord. “Lord” indicates someone who has authority or power over something, so Luke’s use of this title was a fitting acknowledgment that Jesus could do anything because He is Lord over everything—including death itself. Her seemingly hopeless situation changed when she encountered living Hope—Jesus.
answer.zh-Hant: 因為罪的緣故，死亡是每個人生命的一部分，所以耶穌遇見這支送殯隊伍並不令人意外。但對寡婦來說，這一天一切都改變了。她哀傷時，生活仍繼續前行，耶穌卻為她停下。耶穌看見她，為她停下，並顯明祂是主。「主」指對某事有權柄或能力的人，因此路加使用這個稱號，恰當地表明耶穌能做任何事，因為祂是一切的主，包括死亡本身。當她遇見活的盼望——耶穌——時，她看似絕望的處境改變了。

question.en: How does Jesus show us we can hold on to hope, even when we grieve?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌如何向我們顯明，即使在哀傷中，我們仍能持守盼望？

answer.en: Before Adam and Eve chose their own way over God’s way, they enjoyed a home untainted by death and grief. All pain, sickness, and death are the result of sin’s presence in the world. So, in life after the fall, our stories are often colored in the shades of gray that follow unthinkable hurt, tragedy, and loss. But Jesus steps into our moments of deepest pain, as He did for the widow in Nain. When Jesus saw her, His heart was filled with compassion, and He reached out to offer hope. He does the same for us. His offer of salvation not only gives us the hope that comes with freedom from sin and spiritual death but also carries the hope of reuniting us with other believers who have already died. While we experience the heartbreak of living without them on this earth, we can rest in the unshakable truth that because of Jesus, we won’t have to live without them forever.
answer.zh-Hant: 亞當和夏娃選擇自己的道路而不走神的道路之前，享有一個沒有死亡和悲傷玷污的家。一切痛苦、疾病和死亡都是罪存在於世界的結果。因此，在墮落後的生活中，我們的故事常因難以想像的傷痛、悲劇和失去而蒙上灰暗色彩。但耶穌走進我們最深的痛苦時刻，正如祂為拿因城的寡婦所做的一樣。耶穌看見她，心裏充滿憐憫，伸手給她盼望。祂也同樣對待我們。祂所賜的救恩不僅給我們脫離罪和屬靈死亡的盼望，也帶來與其他已離世信徒重聚的盼望。雖然我們在地上經歷沒有他們陪伴的心碎，卻可以安歇於這個不可動搖的真理：因著耶穌，我們不必永遠與他們分離。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌有勝過死亡的權柄

question.en: What did Jesus do to bring the widow’s son back to life? How would you have responded if you saw this miracle?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌做了甚麼，使寡婦的兒子重獲生命？如果你看見這個神蹟，會有甚麼反應？

answer.en: Telling a dead man to get up and actually having it work seems impossible to us. Death seems so final because we don’t have power over it, but we know the One who does. Jesus’s words alone held the power to raise the dead. That’s why He simply commanded a dead man to get up. The man sat up and spoke, and the people were filled with wonder and awe for what Jesus had done. With words, God gave life to the world and everything in it (Heb. 11:3). And with words, Jesus gave life to this widow’s son.
answer.zh-Hant: 吩咐一個死人起來，而且真的發生了，對我們來說似乎不可能。死亡似乎是最終的結局，因為我們沒有能力勝過它，但我們認識那位有能力的主。單憑耶穌的話就有使死人復活的能力，所以祂只需命令死人起來。那人坐起來說話，眾人因耶穌所做的事充滿驚奇和敬畏。神藉著話語將生命賜給世界和其中萬物（希伯來書 11:3）；耶穌也藉著話語把生命賜給這位寡婦的兒子。

question.en: What did Jesus’s power over death do for the people watching? What does it do for us?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌勝過死亡的能力對在場觀看的人產生了甚麼影響？對我們又有甚麼影響？

answer.en: The people who witnessed Jesus raising the widow’s son were amazed and gave glory to God. They believed God had “visited” them, referring to the powerful work Jesus did, not seeing He is God. They saw Jesus the prophet, not Jesus the Savior—Immanuel, “God with us” in the flesh. Yet, their words held a truth they completely missed: God was with them. Here, Jesus proved to them and us that He has the authority to speak and erase death’s power, replacing it with the gift of life. He is more than a great prophet or good teacher; He’s the only One with the power to save us from sin and death.
answer.zh-Hant: 目睹耶穌使寡婦兒子復活的人都感到驚奇，並將榮耀歸給神。他們相信神「眷顧」了他們，這是指耶穌所做的大能之事，卻沒有看出祂就是神。他們看見的是先知耶穌，卻沒有看見救主耶穌——以馬內利，即道成肉身的「神與我們同在」。然而，他們的話包含一個他們完全沒有察覺的真理：神與他們同在。在這裏，耶穌向他們和我們證明，祂有權柄藉著話語除去死亡的權勢，以生命的禮物取而代之。祂不只是一位偉大的先知或良善的老師；祂是唯一有能力拯救我們脫離罪和死亡的主。

question.en: What do we learn about Jesus from His meeting this woman’s need (and ours) before she knew His identity?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌在這位婦人認識祂的身分之前就滿足她的需要，也滿足我們的需要，從中我們對祂有甚麼認識？

answer.en: The widow didn’t ask Jesus for a miracle, but He offered one anyway. He gave her the one thing she desired most, that only He could give: life. Before we knew we needed Him, Jesus came to us while we were trapped in sin and offered us something even greater: eternal life in Him (Rom. 5:8). We have no power to save ourselves, no matter how “good” we are. We can be saved from sin and eternal separation from God only through faith in Jesus and because of His grace toward us. He loved us first. He died to save us. And He “always lives” to intercede for us before the Father (Heb. 7:25). Even when we hadn’t asked for a miracle, Jesus saw our need and stepped in to give us the greatest miracle we never knew we needed: forgiveness from sin, a restored relationship with God, and freedom from spiritual death to live forever in His presence.
answer.zh-Hant: 寡婦沒有向耶穌求神蹟，祂卻主動行了神蹟。祂把她最渴望、也只有祂能給予的東西賜給她：生命。在我們知道自己需要祂之前，耶穌就在我們被罪困住時來到我們當中，賜給我們更大的禮物：在祂裏面的永生（羅馬書 5:8）。無論我們有多「好」，都沒有能力拯救自己。唯有因著耶穌向我們所施的恩典，藉著信靠祂，我們才能從罪和與神永遠隔絕的處境中得救。祂先愛我們，為拯救我們而死，並且「長遠活著」，在天父面前為我們代求（希伯來書 7:25）。即使我們沒有求神蹟，耶穌仍看見我們的需要，介入並賜給我們最大的神蹟，就是我們從不知道自己需要的：罪得赦免、與神的關係恢復，並脫離屬靈的死亡，永遠活在祂面前。

question.en: What are some ways this passage teaches us to encourage people who are grieving? How can you help them know Jesus sees and cares?
question.zh-Hant: 這段經文教導我們可以用哪些方法鼓勵哀傷的人？你如何幫助他們知道耶穌看見並關心他們？

answer.en: Especially if you haven’t experienced grief, trying to comfort someone who’s hurting after a heartbreaking loss can seem intimidating. Even if you’re no stranger to grief, every person handles grief differently, so you still might struggle for the right words to say or the right ways to support your friend. But Jesus shows us some simple ways to help people who are grieving: We can show up; just offering our presence helps. We can see our friends with compassion by providing a safe space for them to talk about their hurt. And instead of letting difficult emotions turn us away, we can come close to offer any practical support they might need (like coffee dates, walks outside, or even a good cry on the couch). If they’re believers, when they’re ready to hear it, we can also gently remind them of the hope we have in Jesus: One day we will be reunited with our loved ones who love Him too. And if they’re not believers, we can lovingly share the hope of the gospel and pray for them and with them.
answer.zh-Hant: 尤其是你自己未曾經歷哀傷時，嘗試安慰因重大損失而傷痛的人，可能會令人望而生畏。即使你對哀傷並不陌生，每個人處理悲傷的方式也不同，所以你仍可能不知道該說甚麼話、用甚麼方式支持朋友。但耶穌向我們示範了一些幫助哀傷之人的簡單方法：我們可以到他們身邊，單是陪伴就有幫助；我們可以帶著憐憫看待朋友，為他們提供安全的空間訴說傷痛。我們也不讓艱難的情緒使自己退開，反而可以靠近他們，提供他們可能需要的實際支持，例如相約喝咖啡、到戶外散步，甚至在沙發上痛哭一場。如果他們是信徒，當他們準備好聆聽時，我們也可以溫柔地提醒他們，我們在耶穌裏有盼望：有一天，我們會與同樣愛祂的親人重聚。如果他們不是信徒，我們可以帶著愛分享福音的盼望，為他們禱告，也與他們一起禱告。

content.en:
What do you do when you mess up? We can easily fix or hide our mistakes with the help of an eraser, the delete key, or a filter. Mistakes in life aren’t so easy to handle, and many leave us wishing we had an undo button for reality, too.

No one knew that feeling better than Adam and Eve. God had given them a specific command: Don’t eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Gen. 2:17). The enemy slithered in and caused them to question God’s goodness and God’s very words. Adam and Eve chose their desire to eat from that tree over God’s plan for them, and they gained knowledge they were never meant to have: awareness of their inadequacy, shame over their nakedness, and fear of God. Without any way to erase their sin, Adam and Eve hid.

Though we may not physically hide from God, we hide when we’re caught in sin too: We lie; we try to cover up our mistakes without coming clean; and we run from God, putting distance between us and Him. Here’s the thing: None of us can hide from the penalty of sin (death), and none of us can hide from the Giver of life (God). So, we might think God’s question, “Where are you?” (Gen. 3:9) is a little odd. But God didn’t ask this question because He lacked knowledge; God asked because He was establishing a pattern of coming to us, of taking the first step, of calling us out to face our sin and see our need for forgiveness. God always sees us; He always seeks us; and He always finds us. And when He does, because of Jesus, believers receive grace and experience the joy of eternal life with God instead of eternal judgment and suffering. What a gift to know that when we sin, we don’t have to hide in the shadows of our shame. We can respond to the Holy Spirit, whose voice draws us out of our sin and into the light.
content.zh-Hant:
你做錯事時會怎樣做？我們可以藉著橡皮擦、刪除鍵或濾鏡，輕易修正或隱藏錯誤。但生活中的錯誤沒那麼容易處理，許多錯誤使我們希望現實生活也有一個復原鍵。

沒有人比亞當和夏娃更了解這種感受。神曾給他們一個明確的命令：不可吃分別善惡樹上的果子（創世記 2:17）。仇敵悄悄潛入，使他們質疑神的良善和祂親口說的話。亞當和夏娃選擇滿足自己吃那棵樹果子的慾望，而不是順從神為他們所定的計劃；他們因此獲得了原本不應有的認知：察覺自己的不足、為赤身露體感到羞恥，以及懼怕神。亞當和夏娃無法抹去自己的罪，只好躲藏起來。

雖然我們未必真的躲起來避開神，但陷在罪中時，我們也會躲藏：我們說謊，試圖掩蓋錯誤而不坦承，並且逃避神，拉開與祂的距離。事實是：我們都無法逃避罪的刑罰，就是死亡；也無法躲避生命的賜予者，就是神。因此，我們可能覺得神的問題「你在哪裏？」（創世記 3:9）有點奇怪。但神問這問題並非因為祂不知道，而是在建立一個模式：祂來尋找我們，踏出第一步，呼喚我們出來面對自己的罪，看見我們需要赦免。神總是看見我們，總是尋找我們，也總能找到我們。當祂找到我們時，因著耶穌，信徒領受恩典，經歷與神同享永生的喜樂，而不是永遠的審判和苦難。知道我們犯罪時不必躲在羞恥的陰影中，是多麼寶貴的禮物！我們可以回應聖靈；祂的聲音引領我們離開罪，進入光明。

question.en: What consequences did God give Adam and Eve for their disobedience (vv. 16-19)?
question.zh-Hant: 神讓亞當和夏娃為他們的不順服承受甚麼後果（第 16-19 節）？

question.en: When confronted with his sin, Adam tried to blame Eve, then God. Where do you place the blame when you sin?
question.zh-Hant: 面對自己的罪時，亞當先怪責夏娃，然後怪責神。你犯罪時會把責任歸給誰？

prayer.en: GOD, THANK YOU FOR LOVING ME FIRST AND COMING TO FIND ME WHEN I WAS LOST IN MY SIN. WITHOUT YOU, I KNOW I’D BE HOPELESS. THANK YOU FOR THE GIFT OF JESUS AND THE HOPE OF ETERNAL LIFE.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢先愛我，並在我迷失於罪中時來尋找我。我知道沒有祢，我就沒有盼望。感謝祢賜下耶穌和永生的盼望。

content.en:
Everyone has different opinions on how to treat wounds and sicknesses. Some might say a deep cut needs stitches, while others might claim duct tape will do the trick (we don’t recommend this). Some believe the best way to get rid of a cold is by taking over-the-counter medicine to reduce symptoms while others consider rest, hydration, and sunlight the best cure. Truthfully, however varied their opinions, only health professionals have the qualifications and knowledge to treat our wounds and illnesses accurately. Our best work is mostly guesswork. The same is true of our sin sickness.

In Genesis 3:16-19, God pronounced sin’s consequences: Adam and Eve worked before the fall to steward God’s good creation, but now they (and all humans) would experience grueling, back-breaking labor and wrestle with the earth to meet their needs; they would endure pain, relational separation from God, and one day, death. However, just before those consequences were pronounced, God gave Adam and Eve a glimpse of hope in what’s considered the first mention of the gospel: One day, Eve’s offspring would strike down the serpent (Satan; see Gen. 3:15). That offspring is Jesus; He is the cure we need (Mark 2:17).

Like Adam and Eve, we can do nothing to save ourselves. No one throughout history has been powerful enough to do that but Jesus, who chose not to save Himself but to die to save us. Jesus explained that the purpose of His presence on earth was to find and save the lost—all of us (Luke 19:10). He accomplished that through His life and ministry on earth, His death on the cross, and His resurrection from the dead. Because of Jesus, we have hope that sin and death are not the end. In Him, we have life and have it fully (John 10:10).
content.zh-Hant:
每個人對如何處理傷口和疾病都有不同意見。有些人可能說深的傷口需要縫合，另一些人卻認為用強力膠帶就可以了（我們不建議這樣做）。有些人相信治療感冒最好的方法是服用非處方藥來減輕症狀，另一些人則認為休息、補充水分和曬太陽是最好的療法。事實上，無論大家的意見多麼不同，只有醫療專業人員具備正確處理傷病的資格和知識。我們盡力而為，大多也只是猜測。我們的罪病也是如此。

在創世記 3:16-19 中，神宣告了罪的後果：亞當和夏娃在墮落之前已有工作，要管理神美好的創造；但現在他們和所有人都要經歷艱苦繁重的勞動，與土地搏鬥以滿足需要；他們要承受痛苦、與神關係的隔絕，並在有一天面臨死亡。然而，就在宣告這些後果之前，神讓亞當和夏娃瞥見一線盼望，這被視為首次提及福音：有一天，夏娃的後裔會擊敗蛇，也就是撒但（見創世記 3:15）。那後裔就是耶穌；祂是我們所需要的醫治（馬可福音 2:17）。

像亞當和夏娃一樣，我們無法拯救自己。歷史上除了耶穌，沒有人有足夠的能力做到；祂選擇不拯救自己，而是受死來拯救我們。耶穌解釋祂來到地上的目的，是尋找和拯救迷失的人，也就是我們所有人（路加福音 19:10）。祂藉著在地上的生命和事工、在十字架上受死，以及從死裏復活，成就了這事。因著耶穌，我們有盼望：罪和死亡並非終結。在祂裏面，我們有生命，並且得著豐盛的生命（約翰福音 10:10）。

question.en: What have you tried to do in the past to stop a specific sin? Why are our efforts not enough?
question.zh-Hant: 過去你曾嘗試做甚麼來停止犯某種罪？為甚麼我們自己的努力不夠？

question.en: How does knowing Jesus could’ve saved Himself from physical death but chose not to so we could have eternal life change your perspective on sin and living for God?
question.zh-Hant: 知道耶穌本可以救自己脫離肉身的死亡，卻選擇不這樣做，使我們可以得著永生，如何改變你對罪和為神而活的看法？

prayer.en: LORD JESUS, THANK YOU FOR WHAT YOU’VE DONE FOR ME, FOR WHAT YOU’RE STILL DOING FOR ME. HELP ME TO BE MORE CONSISTENT IN SHOWING YOU GRATITUDE AND IN LIVING FOR YOU INSTEAD OF GOING MY OWN WAY.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主耶穌，感謝祢為我所做的一切，以及祢仍在為我做的事。幫助我更持續地向祢表達感恩，並為祢而活，而不是走自己的路。

content.en:
Looking away or walking away from chaos and drama takes effort. Maybe you're trying to see why traffic is backed up on the way home from school, watching helplessly as a fight breaks out in the hallway, or seeing someone being attacked on social media. Maybe you wonder, “Isn’t someone going to do something about this?” Or you glance around for the flashing blue lights of a police car, the commanding presence of a coach or teacher, or the rescuing comment to stop the online drama. We want someone to do something about the pain we see and experience.

Life is full of pain. You could be reeling from the death of a loved one, the absence of a parent, the gossip and backstabbing from a good friend, the loss of a dream, or the pressure to excel in school or sports. Sometimes, we don’t even have the words to describe the stress and pain we're feeling. Trying to ask for the help we need can feel overwhelming and intimidating when we're hurting.

Thankfully, Jesus has seen our pain and has done something about it—whether our pain comes from sin we committed, sin committed against us, or the effects of sin on the world and people around us. Not only did He offer us a way to one day be free from the pain of sin and death, but He also sent us His Spirit as a guarantee of this promise and as our Helper and Comforter. Though Jesus Himself isn’t physically walking with us right now, He has given us His presence through the Holy Spirit who lives within us, teaching us, helping us remember what we’ve learned, and praying for us when we don’t have the words.
content.zh-Hant:
面對混亂和衝突時，把目光移開或轉身離去需要努力。也許你正試圖看清放學回家路上為甚麼塞車，或無助地看著走廊上爆發打鬥，或看見有人在社交媒體上受到攻擊。也許你會想：「難道沒有人要做點甚麼嗎？」或者你四處張望，盼望看見警車閃爍的藍燈、教練或老師出面制止，或一則能平息網上紛爭的留言。我們希望有人能處理我們看見和經歷的痛苦。

生活充滿痛苦。你可能正因親人去世、父母一方不在身邊、好友的閒言閒語和背叛、夢想破滅，或在學業或運動上出類拔萃的壓力而深受打擊。有時，我們甚至無法用言語形容所感受的壓力和痛苦。受傷時，嘗試尋求所需的幫助可能令人感到不堪重負、望而生畏。

感謝神，無論我們的痛苦來自自己所犯的罪、別人對我們所犯的罪，還是罪對世界和周圍之人的影響，耶穌都已看見我們的痛苦，並為此採取行動。祂不但為我們預備了一條道路，使我們有一天能脫離罪和死亡的痛苦，還賜下祂的靈作為這應許的保證，並作我們的幫助者和安慰者。雖然耶穌現在沒有親自在肉身中與我們同行，祂卻藉著住在我們裏面的聖靈與我們同在；聖靈教導我們，幫助我們記起所學的，並在我們不知如何表達時為我們禱告。

question.en: Where do you need the reminder that Jesus has seen your pain and has done something about it?
question.zh-Hant: 在甚麼事情上，你需要被提醒耶穌已看見你的痛苦，並為此採取行動？

question.en: What steps can you take to lean into the Holy Spirit’s presence and comfort in your current situation?
question.zh-Hant: 在你目前的處境中，可以採取甚麼步驟，更加依靠聖靈的同在和安慰？

prayer.en: JESUS, THANK YOU FOR DOING SOMETHING ABOUT MY PAIN AND THE PAIN I SEE IN THE WORLD. REMIND ME WHEN I’M HURTING THAT I HAVE THE HOLY SPIRIT LIVING WITHIN ME, ALWAYS READY TO HELP ME AND PRAY FOR ME.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，感謝祢為我的痛苦和我在世界上看見的痛苦採取行動。當我受傷時，求祢提醒我聖靈住在我裏面，隨時準備幫助我、為我禱告。

content.en:
If you've ever been on a roller coaster and quickly figured out that you are not a roller coaster person, you know how endless those loops, heights, drops, and upside-down moments can feel. You know what it’s like to feel trapped until the ride is over and the attendant tells you it’s safe to unfasten the restraints or release the lap bar. Maybe you stumble toward the platform and promise yourself and anyone else who will listen that you will never ride a roller coaster again.

Life can sometimes make us feel like we’re on a roller coaster of struggles and wins, grief and rejoicing. But these heights and drops in life, just like those on a roller coaster, aren’t endless, even if we imagine them that way. God promises that one day, He will wipe our tears and take away death, grief, and pain because the way of our fallen world will pass away (Rev. 21:4). Jesus promised we'd suffer and struggle, but He also promised us hope because He has overcome the world (John 16:33). And that hope is our endless anchor that steadies us when life hurts (Heb. 6:19).

While we hold on to that “one day” hope, God calls us to help others hold on to it too. We might feel like we have nothing to give when we're struggling, but that’s not true. God calls us to give empathy, compassion, and hope—out of the empathy, compassion, and hope He has filled us with through salvation in Jesus and the presence of His Spirit. Out of His endless supply, we can pour into others, drawing their attention to Jesus and His comfort even through our own struggle and pain.
content.zh-Hant:
如果你曾坐過雲霄飛車，並很快發現自己不適合玩這個，你就知道那些迴旋、高處、俯衝和倒轉的時刻會讓人覺得沒完沒了。你知道被困住的感覺，只能等到遊樂設施停下，工作人員告訴你可以安全解開束帶或放開安全壓桿。也許你踉蹌走向乘降平台，向自己和願意聽的人發誓，再也不坐雲霄飛車。

生活有時讓我們覺得自己坐在由掙扎與勝利、悲傷與喜樂交織而成的雲霄飛車上。但生命中的高低起伏就像雲霄飛車一樣，並非無窮無盡，即使我們以為如此。神應許有一天祂要擦去我們的眼淚，除去死亡、悲傷和痛苦，因為我們墮落世界的樣式將要過去（啟示錄 21:4）。耶穌應許我們會受苦、會掙扎，卻也應許我們有盼望，因為祂已勝過世界（約翰福音 16:33）。這盼望是我們永遠穩固的錨，在生命痛苦時使我們穩固（希伯來書 6:19）。

當我們緊抓住這「有一天」的盼望時，神也呼召我們幫助別人持守這盼望。掙扎時，我們可能覺得自己沒有甚麼可給予，但事實並非如此。神呼召我們付出同理、憐憫和盼望，因為祂已藉著耶穌的救恩和聖靈的同在，以這些充滿我們。我們可以從祂無盡的供應中傾注在別人身上，即使在自己的掙扎和痛苦中，也能引導他們注目耶穌和祂的安慰。

question.en: Why is it so important for us to remember that our grief isn’t endless?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼記得我們的悲傷不是無止境的，對我們如此重要？

question.en: What do you think it actually looks like to “weep with those who weep” (Rom. 12:15)? Does someone in your life need you to do this for them?
question.zh-Hant: 你認為「與哀哭的人要同哭」（羅馬書 12:15）在實際生活中是甚麼樣子？你身邊有人需要你這樣陪伴嗎？

prayer.en: FATHER, THANK YOU THAT THE STRUGGLES OF LIFE AREN’T ENDLESS. THANK YOU FOR THE HOPE YOU’VE GIVEN ME FOR THE FUTURE IN JESUS. PLEASE SHOW ME HOW TO COMFORT OTHERS WITH THE COMFORT YOU HAVE GIVEN ME.
prayer.zh-Hant: 天父，感謝祢，生命中的掙扎並非無窮無盡。感謝祢藉著耶穌賜給我對未來的盼望。求祢讓我知道如何用祢賜給我的安慰去安慰別人。

content.en:
Stopping by a welcome center when you enter a state or national park is always a good idea. Rangers stay up to date on weather conditions, road closures, wildlife sightings, fire risks, and trail maintenance. They can help you choose a trail that fits your experience level or your desired outcome—whether you want a physically challenging hike or a relaxing one. They’ll give you a map and some advice and send you on your way. Park rangers can do all this for you because they’ve gone where you’re going; someone else went ahead of them to show them the way, and someone before that mapped out the best paths to take.

Having someone to follow into the unknown is helpful, and death might be the biggest unknown we face. Death comes to all of us, unless Jesus returns before we die. So, death is a “common” experience, yet it can feel so intimidating. We can learn the truth about death and what it means for followers of Jesus, but we don’t know the specifics of what we’ll see and where we’ll be in the moments after we die. But we do know that death for believers isn’t final and that when we’re “away from the body,” we’re “at home with the Lord” (2 Cor. 5:8).

We can be confident in all of this because Jesus is the “firstfruits” of the resurrection (1 Cor. 15:20). The firstfruits are the first and best of the group. He has gone before us in life, in death, and in resurrection. When Jesus tells us He is the only way to have eternal life with God, we can trust Him because He has been there, He has made a way, and He will lead us safely home.
content.zh-Hant:
進入州立或國家公園時，先到遊客中心總是個好主意。公園管理員掌握最新的天氣狀況、道路封閉、野生動物出沒、火災風險和步道維護資訊。他們可以幫你選擇適合你的經驗程度或預期目標的步道，無論你想要有體力挑戰的健行，還是輕鬆漫步。他們會給你地圖和建議，然後讓你出發。公園管理員能為你做這一切，是因為他們曾走過你要走的路；在他們之前有人帶路，而更早以前也有人繪出最佳的路徑。

在進入未知領域時有人可以跟隨，是很有幫助的；死亡可能是我們面對的最大未知。除非耶穌在我們死之前再來，否則死亡會臨到我們每一個人。所以死亡是「普遍」的經歷，卻仍可能令人望而生畏。我們可以認識有關死亡的真理，以及死亡對耶穌跟隨者的意義，但我們不知道死後那一刻會看見甚麼、身處何處等細節。不過我們知道，死亡對信徒而言並非終結；當我們「離開身體」，就是「與主同住」（哥林多後書 5:8）。

我們能確信這一切，是因為耶穌是復活「初熟的果子」（哥林多前書 15:20）。初熟的果子是收成中最先、最好的部分。祂在生命、死亡和復活中都走在我們前面。耶穌告訴我們，祂是與神同享永生的唯一道路時，我們可以信靠祂，因為祂去過那裏，祂已開了一條路，並會領我們平安回家。

question.en: Who would you follow anywhere, no matter what? Why?
question.zh-Hant: 無論如何，你會跟隨誰到任何地方？為甚麼？

question.en: How does Jesus’s going before us in death and resurrection give you hope for the future?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌在死亡和復活中走在我們前面，如何給你對未來的盼望？

prayer.en: Father, help me to trust that You mean what You say. Thank You for giving me victory over death through Jesus. Show me how to live like I believe my home is ultimately with You.
prayer.zh-Hant: 天父，求祢幫助我相信祢說的話都是真實的。感謝祢藉著耶穌使我勝過死亡。求祢指示我如何活出信心，相信我最終的家是在祢那裏。
